two_sentence_summary: Feste and Ledger introduce Build While Bleeding as the umbrella for four distinct projects: Hardwire, Seuss, The Leak Report, and Cartography. They explain each project briefly and place Ring My Bell within the larger body of work as a research-driven audio show.

projects.name: Hardwire
projects.purpose: Practical music theory for rappers, beatmakers, and self-taught producers; FEEL, MAP, CONTROL.

projects.name: Seuss
projects.purpose: Rhythm, meter, cadence, syncopation, rhyme patterns, and language in hip-hop.

projects.name: The Leak Report
projects.purpose: Examines communication, assumptions, claims, context, and evidence.

projects.name: Cartography
projects.purpose: Preserves music, lyrics, writing, and documents as a creative and narrative archive.

projects.name: Ring My Bell
projects.purpose: Turns topics and source material into researched, two-host talk-radio episodes.

editorial_note: Build While Bleeding is the umbrella; the projects beneath it remain distinct. Their shared purpose is to develop useful ideas, examine them carefully, and preserve the work. A difficult origin or polished presentation is not proof of quality; each project must stand on its own merits.
audio_note: The local audio draft uses eSpeak voices and a restrained synthetic tonal bed. It is a functional preview, not the final Gemini/Lyria studio-quality pipeline output.
